title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 3.3 Healing of Blind Bartimaeus

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Mark 10:46-52 tells how blind Bartimaeus cried out to Jesus near Jericho and received his sight. In this sub-strand you will retell that healing, see the faith Bartimaeus showed, and thank Jesus for His power over sickness and disease.

## Strand 3.0: The Life of Jesus Christ
Sub-strand 3.3: Healing of Blind Bartimaeus
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) retell the healing of blind Bartimaeus
b) recognise the healing power of Jesus Christ in their lives
c) appreciate Jesus’ power over sickness and disease

## Key inquiry questions
1. How did Bartimaeus show faith in Jesus Christ?

## Core competencies
• Learning to Learn: the skill of sharing experiences is enhanced as learners share an incident when they prayed to God for healing.
• Communication: the skill of speaking clearly and effectively is portrayed as learners retell the healing of blind Bartimaeus.

## Values
• Responsibility: learners engage in assigned roles and duties as they role-play the healing of blind Bartimaeus.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Health Issues: non-communicable diseases- blindness: Bartimaeus was blind but he was healed.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: reading skills are applied as they read and learn new vocabulary.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing and role play.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 3.0 The Life of Jesus Christ, Sub-strand 3.3 Healing of Blind Bartimaeus
• Mark 10:46-52

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: What happened at Jericho

LESSON 1: WHAT HAPPENED AT JERICHO
==================================

## What you will learn
• Retell the healing of blind Bartimaeus from Mark 10:46-52.
• Put the events in the correct order.

Curriculum outcomes: a) retell the healing of blind Bartimaeus

## Introduction
A blind man sitting by a road cannot see the crowd, but he can hear a name. Bartimaeus heard that Jesus of Nazareth was passing, and he refused to stay quiet.

## Notes
Read Mark 10:46-52 and retell it in this order.

Jesus and His disciples were leaving Jericho with a large crowd. A blind man, Bartimaeus, which means son of Timaeus, was sitting by the roadside begging.

When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to shout, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" Many people rebuked him and told him to be quiet. He shouted even louder, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"

Jesus stopped and said, "Call him." They called the blind man and said, "Cheer up! On your feet! He is calling you." Bartimaeus threw his cloak aside, jumped up, and came to Jesus.

Jesus asked, "What do you want me to do for you?" The blind man said, "Rabbi, I want to see."

Jesus said, "Go, your faith has healed you." Immediately Bartimaeus received his sight and followed Jesus along the road.

### Details to keep straight
- The place was Jericho, as Jesus was leaving the city.
- Bartimaeus was blind and he was begging.
- He called Jesus "Son of David" and asked for mercy.
- The crowd tried to silence him. He shouted more.
- He left his cloak behind when Jesus called.
- He asked to see. Jesus said his faith had healed him.
- He followed Jesus.

Do not add another miracle to this retelling. Speak clearly so a listener who has not read the passage can see the scene. Then role-play it and, if the teacher allows, record the role-play on a digital device.

## Key words
• mercy — kind help given to someone in need, which Bartimaeus asked from Jesus
• Rabbi — a title meaning teacher, which Bartimaeus used for Jesus
• Son of David — the title Bartimaeus shouted, naming Jesus as the promised descendant of David

## Activity: Read and role-play the healing
You will need: Bible, A cloth to use as a cloak, Digital device if the teacher provides one
1. Sing a song about the healing power of God.
2. Read Mark 10:46-52 and retell the healing of blind Bartimaeus.
3. Role-play the story: Bartimaeus, the crowd, Jesus and the disciples.
4. Record the role-play on a digital device if one is available, and play it back to check the order of events.

## Practice
1. Where was Bartimaeus, and what was he doing?
2. What did he shout, and what did the crowd do?
3. What did Jesus say had healed Bartimaeus?

## Summary
• Blind Bartimaeus begged by the road as Jesus left Jericho.
• He kept calling for mercy until Jesus called him.
• He asked to see, received his sight, and followed Jesus.

### Answers to practice
1. He was sitting by the roadside at Jericho, begging. He was blind.
2. He shouted, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" Many people told him to be quiet, but he shouted even more.
3. His faith. Jesus said, "Your faith has healed you," and immediately he could see.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Faith and the healing power of Jesus

LESSON 2: FAITH AND THE HEALING POWER OF JESUS
==============================================

## What you will learn
• Explain how Bartimaeus showed faith.
• Recognise the healing power of Jesus in the lives of believers.

Curriculum outcomes: b) recognise the healing power of Jesus Christ in their lives

## Introduction
Jesus did not say that the crowd healed Bartimaeus. He said, "Your faith has healed you." Faith was the hand Bartimaeus reached out with.

## Notes
Faith is trusting Jesus enough to act on that trust. Bartimaeus showed faith in several ways that Mark 10 records.

- He believed Jesus could help, so he shouted instead of staying silent.
- He did not stop when people told him to be quiet.
- He used a title of honour, "Son of David," and asked for mercy.
- When Jesus called, he threw his cloak aside and came at once. He did not cling to the cloth he had been sitting on.
- He said exactly what he needed: "I want to see."
- After he was healed, he followed Jesus.

### Healing power
The healing was immediate. Blind eyes received sight. That power belongs to Jesus. Christians recognise it when they pray for the sick and when they thank God for recovery. Recognise means to see and admit that the power is His.

Share an incident when you, or your family, prayed to God for healing. You do not need to invent a result. Tell what you asked and how you trusted Him. Some people are healed at once, as Bartimaeus was. Some keep praying. In both cases the power is Jesus' power, not ours.

You show faith in ordinary sickness by praying, taking the right medicine a parent or doctor gives, resting, and thanking God. Faith does not tell you to hide a serious illness. Tell an adult, pray, and trust Jesus.

## Key words
• faith — trusting Jesus enough to call on Him and obey
• healing — being made well from sickness, as Bartimaeus received his sight

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A friend says Bartimaeus was healed because the crowd felt sorry for him. What does Mark 10:52 say?

Working:
1. Jesus stopped because of the man's cry.
2. Jesus said, "Your faith has healed you."
3. The crowd had tried to silence him.

Answer: Jesus said Bartimaeus' faith had healed him. The crowd had told him to be quiet.

## Activity: Share a time of prayer for healing
You will need: Bible
1. List the actions that show Bartimaeus' faith.
2. Each learner shares an incident when he or she prayed to God for healing.
3. The class listens with respect and does not laugh.
4. Sing a song about the healing power of Jesus.

## Practice
1. Give two ways Bartimaeus showed faith.
2. Who has power to heal, according to this story?
3. What should a sick learner do besides praying?

## Summary
• Bartimaeus showed faith by calling out, refusing to be silenced, and asking to see.
• Jesus said, "Your faith has healed you."
• Christians pray to Jesus, whose healing power is real.

### Answers to practice
1. Any two: he shouted to Jesus, he would not be silenced, he came at once when called, he asked to see, he followed Jesus.
2. Jesus.
3. Tell a parent or doctor, take the right medicine, and rest, while still trusting Jesus.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Jesus' power over sickness and disease

LESSON 3: JESUS' POWER OVER SICKNESS AND DISEASE
================================================

## What you will learn
• Appreciate Jesus' power over sickness and disease.
• Show care for people who are blind or ill.

Curriculum outcomes: c) appreciate Jesus’ power over sickness and disease

## Introduction
Blindness is a serious condition. Bartimaeus could not see the road or the faces around him. Jesus' power reached that sickness and ended it. Christians appreciate that power and treat sick people with kindness.

## Notes
Sickness and disease are part of life in this world. Blindness meant Bartimaeus had to beg by the road. People could have walked past. Jesus stopped. Appreciating His power means you do not treat healing as luck. You thank Him.

### What the miracle shows
- Jesus has power over sickness. Blind eyes were opened immediately.
- He has time for one person in a large crowd.
- He asks people to say what they need.
- Faith and healing belong together in this story.
- A healed person can follow Him. Bartimaeus did.

### How to appreciate the power
- Thank Jesus when you or someone you love recovers.
- Pray for the sick by name.
- Sing songs about His healing power.
- Do not mock a person who cannot see, cannot hear, or cannot walk. Bartimaeus was blind, and the crowd told him to be quiet. Do not be that crowd.
- Help a classmate who is ill by sharing notes or visiting with a parent's permission.
- Tell a teacher if you notice a learner who needs medical help.

Health includes care of the eyes: read in good light, do not throw objects at faces, and tell an adult if your eyes hurt. These habits do not replace Jesus' power. They are wise ways of looking after the body He made. When disease comes, you still pray, because He is Lord over sickness.

## Key words
• disease — a sickness that harms the body
• appreciate — to value and give thanks for something
• blindness — being unable to see, as Bartimaeus was before Jesus healed him

## Activity: Thank Jesus and show kindness
You will need: Exercise book
1. Write a short thank-you prayer for Jesus' power over sickness.
2. List kind actions toward a person who is blind or ill.
3. Role-play helping a blind classmate move safely across the room, with care and permission.
4. Sing a song about the healing power of God.

## Practice
1. What sickness did Jesus heal in Mark 10:46-52?
2. How can you appreciate Jesus' power over disease?
3. What was wrong with the crowd's first response to Bartimaeus?

## Summary
• Jesus has power over sickness and disease.
• Bartimaeus was blind and was healed immediately.
• Appreciate that power by giving thanks and by being kind to people who are ill.

### Answers to practice
1. Blindness. Bartimaeus received his sight immediately.
2. By thanking Him, praying for the sick, and not mocking people who are ill.
3. They told him to be quiet instead of helping him reach Jesus.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 3.3 HEALING OF BLIND BARTIMAEUS
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. The healing of Bartimaeus is told in...
   A. Mark 10:46-52
   B. Luke 17:11-19
   C. Genesis 12:1-5
   D. John 3:16

2. Bartimaeus was sitting...
   A. on a throne
   B. by the roadside begging
   C. in a boat
   D. in a tree

3. He called Jesus...
   A. Son of David
   B. king of Moab
   C. Pharaoh
   D. a tax collector

4. When people told him to be quiet, Bartimaeus:
   A. went home
   B. shouted even more
   C. cursed them
   D. fell asleep

5. What did he ask Jesus to do?

6. Jesus said Bartimaeus was healed by...
   A. the crowd's pity
   B. his faith
   C. his cloak
   D. the dust of the road

7. After he received his sight, Bartimaeus:
   A. returned to begging
   B. followed Jesus along the road
   C. climbed a tree
   D. left Jericho without a word

8. Recognising Jesus' healing power means:

9. Which action appreciates Jesus' power over disease?
   A. Mocking a blind person
   B. Thanking Jesus and praying for the sick
   C. Telling a sick person to be quiet
   D. Refusing all help from adults

10. Blindness in this story is an example of:
   A. a sickness Jesus has power over
   B. a punishment the class should copy
   C. something faith cannot bring to Jesus
   D. a reason to stay silent
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 3.3 HEALING OF BLIND BARTIMAEUS
========================================

1. A. Mark 10:46-52
   The class reads Mark 10:46-52.

2. B. by the roadside begging
   Mark 10:46 says he was sitting by the roadside begging as Jesus left Jericho.

3. A. Son of David
   He shouted, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"

4. B. shouted even more
   Mark 10:48 says he shouted all the more.

5. He said, "Rabbi, I want to see."
   Mark 10:51 records his request.

6. B. his faith
   Mark 10:52: "Your faith has healed you."

7. B. followed Jesus along the road
   Mark 10:52 says he followed Jesus along the road.

8. Admitting that He is able to heal and praying to Him when people are sick.
   The power in the story is His, not the crowd's.

9. B. Thanking Jesus and praying for the sick
   Thanks and prayer honour His power. Mockery copies the crowd that tried to silence Bartimaeus.

10. A. a sickness Jesus has power over
   Bartimaeus was blind, and Jesus healed him. That shows power over sickness.
